earlier_scan.note: Extinct Southern Alakaluf; Glottolog lists only early vocabularies (Fitz-Roy 1839; Hyades & Deniker 1891) and Viegas Barros comparative notes; nothing on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record alac1239 (JSON): Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Hyades & Deniker 1891; Fitz-Roy 1839); Ethnologue-comment citing Viegas Barros 1990 and 2005 for the recognition of a distinct Southern Alakaluf language.
sources.note: n/a; confirms no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for this variety.

sources.citation: Cooper, John M. 1917. Analytical and critical bibliography of the tribes of Tierra del Fuego and adjacent territory. Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 63. Washington: GPO. (archive.org item analyticalcritic00coop, scanned text)
sources.note: Explicitly negative: p.4 'of Alacalufan grammar we know not a single rule'; p.10 'Nothing has thus far been published on Alacalufan grammar.. We are obliged, therefore, to confine our comparative study to the available lexical material.'

sources.citation: de Mauro, Sofía. 2023. 'Capítulo 1. Lenguas fueguinas: Thomas Bridges y Bartolomé Mitre' [edition of Bridges's 1898 letter to Mitre]. In Malvestitti & Farro (eds.), Documentos inéditos en lenguas fuegopatagónicas (1880-1950), 67-86. Viedma: Editorial UNRN. DOI 10.4000/books.eunrn.22237.
sources.note: Nothing; historiographic chapter on Bridges and Mitre; the austral Alakaluf variety is only named in a classificatory footnote.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, Jose Pedro & Marisa Malvestitti. 2023. Capitulo 2. Vocabulario ona-yahgan-alakaluf del doctor Carlos Spegazzini. In Marisa Malvestitti & Maximo Farro (eds.), Documentos ineditos en lenguas fuegopatagonicas (1880-1950), 87-135. Viedma: Editorial UNRN. ISBN 978-987-8258-34-8. doi:10.4000/books.eunrn.22242 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0).
sources.note: Nothing. direct download string search over the whole chapter (body, notes, tables) found zero occurrences of 'acent', 'tonic', 'prosod', 'intensidad', 'entonac'. Notation paragraph covers only Italian/Spanish letter values, diaeresis and circumflex; Spegazzini's acute accents on alakaluf forms (affalaku, tshilkoa, tlello, seciol, celukl in tablas 2.7-2.8) are reproduced but not interpreted. New open primary-source edition for alac1239, silent on stress.

sources.citation: Regunaga, Maria Alejandra. 2022. Los metodos de transcripcion del yagan en las expediciones cientificas del siglo XIX. Revista argentina de historiografia linguistica 14(1): 31-51.
sources.note: Second-hand description of Fitz-Roy's notation: the apostrophe/prime is a syllabic accent mark, breve and tilde mark quantity; Despard 1859 later dropped the accents. Nothing on where the accent falls in Alikhoolip.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro & Marisa Malvestitti. 2019. Un manuscrito de Carlos Spegazzini con datos ineditos sobre la lengua haush. Indiana 36(2): 101-128, with 'Apendice' A117-A137. Berlin: Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut. doi:10.18441/ind.v36i2.101-128 (CC BY-NC-ND).
sources.note: Nothing on Alakaluf; Haush phonetics only. Kept as the companion documenting the manuscript source of the Southern Alakaluf (Sahualkis) wordlist.

sources.citation: Aguilera F., Oscar E. 2017. El nombre kawesqar, un problema no solo linguistico. Magallania 45(1): 75-84.
sources.note: No phonology content; relevant only to identity (one language vs three).

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro. 2016. Los numerales de la lengua yagan. Cuadernos de la ALFAL 9: 48-63.
sources.note: Only a Yagan remark (suffixes generally unaccented in Yagan; accent on final syllable in kəmpay); nothing on Alakaluf accent.

sources.note: No phonology; bibliographic pointer only.

sources.citation: Clairis, Christos. 1997. Linguistica fueguina 1997. In: Actas de las Terceras Jornadas de Linguistica Aborigen, 21-44. Buenos Aires: UBA, Instituto de Linguistica (also Onomazein 2: 421-450).
sources.note: Phonology content is a segmental comparison of the seven Fuegian systems (plain vs glottalized stops, qawasqar aspirated series, fricative series, three vowel qualities); no mention of accent/stress for any variety.
sources.venue: Actas de las Terceras Jornadas de Linguistica Aborigen

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, Jose Pedro. 1996. Transferencia lexica en Tierra del Fuego. Signo y Sena 6: 513-531. Buenos Aires: Universidad de Buenos Aires, Facultad de Filosofia y Letras. doi:10.34096/sys.n6.5729
sources.note: No statement about accent in Southern (or any) qawasqar. The only prosodic remark: Selk'nam forms with 'irregular' second-syllable intensity accent (e.g. apums 'a fish') may be Yagan loans, i.e. Selk'nam would have borrowed a Yagan accentuation pattern. Southern qawasqar forms are cited in the compilers' spellings with Fitz-Roy's marks but not analysed prosodically.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro. 1994. Explorando la hipotesis de parentesco alacalufe-yagan. Lengua y Literatura Mapuche 6: 281-285. Temuco: Universidad de La Frontera (now served by Revista de Lenguas y Literatura Indoamericanas, art. 150; CC BY 4.0).
sources.note: No mention of acento/stress; phonological section purely segmental. Shows Viegas Barros's phonemicization of the Southern corpus carries no accent marking in citation, which lowers (but does not settle) the odds that his 1991/2005 works state an S accent rule.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, Jose Pedro. 1990. Dialectologia qawasqar. Amerindia 15. Paris: A.E.A.
sources.note: Defines the Southern variety S (Brecknock Peninsula = Fitz-Roy's alikhoolip; sources Fitz-Roy, Hyades, Spegazzini; c.350 lexical items); sec. 3.4 phoneme system of N (from Clairis 1987) and sec. 3.5 N:C:S consonant and vowel correspondences; purely segmental, no mention of acento/stress (only hit for 'acentua-' is non-linguistic, p. near fn.28).

sources.citation: Clairis, Christos. 1985. The Indigenous Languages of Tierra del Fuego. In Harriet E. Manelis Klein & Louisa R. Stark (eds.), South American Indian Languages: Retrospect and Prospect, 753-783. Austin: University of Texas Press.
sources.note: No phonology content (names, territories, research history, genetic hypotheses, large bibliography).

sources.citation: Gusinde, Martin. 1926. Das Lautsystem der feuerlaendischen Sprachen. Anthropos 21(5-6): 1000-1024 (sec. I Selk'nam, II 'Das Lautsystem der Halakwulup' pp. 1010-1017, III Yamana).
sources.note: Segment inventory in Anthropos notation; individual vowels characterised as occurring 'betont'/'unbetont' (e.g. 'e tritt fast nur als unbetonter Vokal auf'; a 'meist sehr stark betont, wie es ueberhaupt in den haeufigsten Faellen die Betonung fuehrt'), and the quiet, lax articulation of the language is described; no statement locating word accent. (Same finding as the alac1240 check of this file.)

sources.citation: Lehmann-Nitsche, Robert. 1921 (dated 1919). El grupo linguistico alakaluf de los canales magallanicos. Revista del Museo de La Plata 25: 15-69; appendix prints Spegazzini's unpublished 1882 Alakaluf vocabularies I (informant Sahualkis, Brecknock Peninsula) and II (Banerko, Darwin Cove), pp. 59-62. (archive.org item revistadelmuseo251921univ, scanned text of the tome)
sources.note: p.46: the Spegazzini lists are given in 'una transcripcion mas o menos fonetica' with Italian orthography; individual words bear acute accents (yauas 'acqua' written yáuas, ákis, tetél, átupil, táhhlióla) but no statement about accent placement; no 'acento' anywhere in the article.
sources.venue: Revista del Museo de La Plata

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1891. The American Race: A Linguistic Classification and Ethnographic Description of the Native Tribes of North and South America. New York: N. D. C. Hodges (archive.org copy of the 1901 Philadelphia: McKay printing, identifier americanraceling00brinrich; scanned text).
sources.note: Nothing on accent; only 'The Yahgan and Alikuluf pass for independent stocks. Yet in a number of words they resemble each other..' (p.364 note). Wordlist column without any prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Hyades, Paul & Joseph Deniker. 1891. Mission scientifique du Cap Horn 1882-1883, tome VII: Anthropologie, ethnographie. Paris: Gauthier-Villars. Chapter 'Langage', Alakalouf vocabularies pp. 272-279. (archive.org item missionscientifi71891miss, scanned text)
sources.note: Three comparative wordlists only (Orange Bay Alakalouf woman vs Fitz-Roy's Alikhoolip; Dr Fenton's list checked with the boy Cyrille at Punta Arenas); closing remark p.279 that the differences 'prouvent peut-etre.. l'existence de plusieurs dialectes chez les Alakalouf'; nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Fitz-Roy, Robert. 1839. Narrative of the surveying voyages of His Majesty's ships Adventure and Beagle, vol. II, Appendix, 'Fragment of a vocabulary of the Alikhoolip and the Tekeenica languages', pp. 135-140. London: Colburn. (archive.org item narrativeofsurve21839fitz, scanned text)
sources.note: p.135 preface gives only vowel/consonant letter values ('the vowels should be sounded as in the English syllables bah, bat, eel..'); the Alikhoolip words carry an apostrophe accent mark after a syllable (yok'cushlu, acil'labe, t'quim'be) but no rule or explanation of the mark is stated anywhere in the appendix (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing relevant).
sources.venue: II, Appendix, 'Fragment of a vocabulary of the Alikhoolip and the Tekeenica languages'
